name: Tarsal Coalition
definition: Abnormal fibrous, cartilaginous or bony connection between tarsal bones that can cause rigid flatfoot, pain and recurrent ankle sprains, often becoming symptomatic in adolescence.

investigations.principle: CT defines bony coalition; MRI helps fibrous/cartilaginous coalition; radiographs may show characteristic signs.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Persistent symptomatic coalition may require resection or corrective surgery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Pada-Sandhi congenital/developmental phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Abnormal fibrous, cartilaginous or bony connection between tarsal bones that can cause rigid flatfoot, pain and recurrent ankle sprains, often becoming symptomatic in adolescence.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
